title: Series Splitting Representation vs RFC 5545 RANGE=THISANDFUTURE

citations.verbatim_quote: The parameter specifies the effective range of recurrence instances that is specified by the property. The effective range is from the recurrence identifier specified by the property. If this parameter is not specified on an allowed property, then the default range is the single instance specified by the recurrence identifier value of the property. The parameter value can only be "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate a range defined by the recurrence identifier and all subsequent instances.

Assuming an unbounded recurring calendar component scheduled to occur on Mondays and Wednesdays, the "RANGE" parameter could not be used to reschedule only the future Monday instances to occur on Tuesday instead. In such cases, the calendar application could simply truncate the unbounded recurring calendar component (i.e., with the "COUNT" or "UNTIL" rule parts), and create two new unbounded recurring calendar components for the future instances.
If present, this JSCalendar object represents one occurrence of a recurring JSCalendar object. If present, the "recurrenceRules" and "recurrenceOverrides" properties MUST NOT be present.

A VEVENT (or VTODO) component is a recurrence override if it has the RECURRENCE-ID property set, and the iCalendar object contains a VEVENT (or VTODO) component that does not have the RECURRENCE-ID but the RRULE property set, and the UID property values of the two components are equal. The component without the RECURRENCE-ID property is in that case referred to as the "main component".
The RANGE parameter [RFC5545] (Section 3.2.13) does not convert to a standard JSCalendar element. Implementations MAY preserve it in the iCalendar (Section 5.1.1) property.

rationale: RFC 5545 defines two mechanisms for modifying a recurrence instance and all subsequent instances: (1) specifying RECURRENCE-ID;RANGE=THISANDFUTURE on an overriding component for uniform start/duration shifts (Section 3.2.13 and Section 3.8.4.4), and (2) truncating the prior recurring calendar component using UNTIL or COUNT and creating a new recurring calendar component for the future instances when modifying recurrence rules or complex schedules (Section 3.8.4.4 Note). Modern CalExt specifications (RFC 8984 Section 4.3.1 and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Section 2.1.2 / 2.3.34) deprecate RANGE=THISANDFUTURE in the data model entirely—forbidding recurrenceRules on an override object with recurrenceId—and instead model a split series as a bounded prior recurring component plus a separate recurring component for the future series. As an abstract STORE_POLICY, a calendar store may represent THIS_AND_FUTURE edits on non-first instances by truncating the existing master component's RRULE with UNTIL and forking a new recurring component in the same calendar that retains the original UID, sets RECURRENCE-ID to the split occurrence identifier (without a RANGE=THISANDFUTURE parameter), increments SEQUENCE, updates CREATED/DTSTAMP/LAST-MODIFIED to the edit revision timestamp, and carries the future RRULE.
store_implication: When an edit operation with THIS_AND_FUTURE range is invoked for an occurrence strictly after the master component's DTSTART: (1) Component state: the prior recurring component must have its RRULE truncated strictly before the split RECURRENCE-ID (clearing COUNT and setting UNTIL to the inclusive bound immediately preceding the split instance) and its DTSTAMP/LAST-MODIFIED updated; a new recurring component must be inserted sharing the same UID, with RECURRENCE-ID set to the split occurrence identifier, SEQUENCE incremented (from the prior component's SEQUENCE, or 1 if 0/unset), CREATED/DTSTAMP/LAST-MODIFIED set to the edit timestamp, DTSTART set to the new start (or the split occurrence's original start timestamp), and RRULE set to the future recurrence rule (retaining only EXDATE values that remain valid occurrences of the forked future series). (2) Timeline state: recurrence expansion expands both the truncated prior component and the forked future recurring component (since recurring components with an RRULE are expanded as series rather than treated as single-instance overrides), yielding the prior occurrences before the split point followed seamlessly by the new series occurrences from the split point onward.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Strict JSCalendar (RFC 8984 Section 4.3.1) forbids both recurrenceId and recurrenceRules on the same object; this STORE_POLICY retains both RECURRENCE-ID and RRULE on the forked future VEVENT/VTODO with the same UID so that components belonging to the split family remain grouped by UID.

If the original series has EXDATE values falling in the future range, only EXDATE values that still align with valid occurrences of the forked future series are retained on the forked component; EXDATEs belonging to the prior segment or invalidated by a start-time shift are pruned.

If the series is split multiple times at progressively later recurrence identifiers, each split truncates the currently active segment's RRULE UNTIL bound and inserts another recurring segment component sharing the same UID.

If the edit also changes the recurrence rule (e.g., changing FREQ=WEEKLY to FREQ=DAILY from the split point onward), truncating the prior component and forking a new recurring component cleanly represents the schedule change, which RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 notes cannot be represented by RANGE=THISANDFUTURE alone.

scenarios.name: split_weekly_series_this_and_future_summary_change
scenarios.description: Editing the second occurrence of a 3-instance weekly series with THIS_AND_FUTURE range truncates the original component with UNTIL and forks a new recurring component starting at the second occurrence.

audit_notes: Scrubbed all implementation references and internal module/function names to enforce 100% clean-room specification.

Contextual RFC check (+/- 40 lines): Verified RFC 5545 Section 3.2.13 (L1323-L1330), Section 3.8.4.4 Note (L6454-L6461), RFC 8984 Section 4.3.1 (L1069-L1071), and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Sections 2.1.2 (L609-L614) & 2.3.34 (L3618-L3620).

Authority check: Confirmed STORE_POLICY is accurate because choosing series truncation + forked recurring component sharing the same UID and RECURRENCE-ID (rather than emitting RECURRENCE-ID;RANGE=THISANDFUTURE or minting a new UID) is a store representation policy.
